sections.h2: What is different about selling a house in Cherry Hill, NJ?
sections.html:
Cherry Hill sellers deal with two separate township inspections before closing, one for the property's exterior and one for smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, and both are scheduled through different offices. Booking both early keeps the closing date from slipping.

The township is large, mostly owner-occupied and built largely in the decades after World War II, so the typical seller owns a single-family house on a suburban lot with trees, fences, driveways and sidewalks that the township cares about. This page walks through the inspections, the tax calendar, the county recording fees and a worked transfer-fee example so you can set a realistic closing date.

sections.h2: How big is Cherry Hill and how did it develop?
sections.html:
Cherry Hill covers about 24 square miles of Camden County, which makes it the largest municipality in the county by population. It began as Delaware Township in 1844, and in 1961 took the Cherry Hill name from a local farm. Quaker settlers arrived in the late 1600s, the first small cluster was Colestown, and 19th-century farms supplied produce to the Campbell's soup plant across the river in Camden. Population then jumped after World War II, from about 10,400 in 1950 to 31,500 in 1960 and 64,400 in 1970.

Its neighborhoods include Ashland, Barclay, Erlton, Greentree, Kingston Estates, Springdale, Woodcrest and the area around Cherry Hill Mall. Pennsauken Creek marks the eastern line with Burlington County, the Cooper River runs along the southern border beside Route 70, and Haddonfield, Collingswood and Voorhees sit across those lines.

sections.h2: Which roads, transit lines and schools matter to Cherry Hill buyers?
sections.html:
Cherry Hill is built around highway access to Philadelphia. Interstate 295 has three exits in the township, including exit 31, which leads directly to the Woodcrest PATCO station, and Routes 38, 41, 70 and 154 cross it. The township's roads total about 309 miles, of which the township itself maintains roughly 247. NJ Transit runs buses to Philadelphia on the 317, 404 and 406 routes, and the Atlantic City Line stops at the Cherry Hill station.

Schools are the other big talking point. Cherry Hill Public Schools operates 19 schools, with about 10,800 students in the 2023 to 2024 school year, including two traditional high schools, Cherry Hill High School East and Cherry Hill High School West, three middle schools and 12 elementary schools. Private options include Camden Catholic High School and the King's Christian School.

  • Mention the PATCO station and I-295 exits in your listing if you are close to them.
  • Name the elementary school zone, since buyers search by it.
  • Note the Cooper River or creek frontage if the lot touches one and have any drainage history ready.

sections.h2: What are the two Cherry Hill inspections before closing?
sections.html:
A Cherry Hill home seller needs a Certificate of Continued Occupancy from the township and a smoke alarm and carbon monoxide compliance certificate from the fire department. Both are required before a single-family sale can reach closing, and they are separate appointments with separate fees.

The occupancy certificate is issued by Community Development, which handles property maintenance, at 820 Mercer Street, Room 202. The property maintenance officer inspects the exterior areas only. The township lists these items:

  • Sidewalks, driveways and fences.
  • Trees and natural growth.
  • Sanitation and exhaust vents.
  • Grading and drainage, including where sump pumps discharge.
  • Accessory structures and ground surface hazards.

The inspection costs $100, due before the inspector comes, and you can apply online, in person or by mail. Online applications need office approval before the payment request is emailed, there are no refunds after payment if you cancel, and the property maintenance line is 856-834-3364. Some condominiums and townhomes are excluded, and the township posts a list of properties that skip the inspection.

The fire department certificate is a different step. It is required for one- and two-family homes before settlement, and the township asks sellers to request the appointment three to four weeks ahead. The certificate is issued on the spot if the home passes and payment is made, temporary certificates are not issued, and fire extinguishers are no longer required. The fire department's inspection line is (856) 429-7441. Since the two appointments run on separate calendars, book both the week the contract is signed.

sections.h2: Does the township help with move-out trash after a Cherry Hill sale?
sections.html:
Yes, Cherry Hill offers a one-time courtesy collection for house clean-outs after a sale, covering furniture, carpets, bedding and similar household items. Proof that you applied for a Continued Certificate of Occupancy is required before the Department of Public Works will schedule it, pickups are on Fridays, and you call 856-424-4422 to book one.

The same guidelines say no trash or recycling collection goes to dwellings under construction, vacant lots or properties without a valid certificate of occupancy, so a vacant house waiting on its paperwork may be left without service. Plan the clean-out around the certificate date, and keep contractor debris out of the cart, because contractor-generated construction waste has to be hauled by the contractor.

sections.h2: When are Cherry Hill property taxes due and who collects them?
sections.html:
Cherry Hill property tax is due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1, with a ten-day grace period that rolls to the next business day if it ends on a weekend or holiday. The township mails bills twice a year, in July for the third and fourth quarters and in January for the first and second. Payments must arrive in the tax office by the last day of grace, because postmarks are not accepted.

Interest on late payments runs at 8 percent a year on the first $1,500 and 18 percent on anything above that, counted from the original due date. The tax collector also bills sewer rent: residential sewer is a flat annual fee due April 1, with a 10 percent discount for owners 60 or older who live in the property. Ask the tax office at 856-488-7880 for a closing figure that includes any sewer balance. The office collects for the school district, the fire district and Camden County along with the township, so the bill you pay includes those shares.

Appeals follow state deadlines: April 1, or May 1 where a revaluation has been done, filed with the Camden County Board of Taxation.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer fee and where is the deed recorded?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Camden County Clerk, and the seller owes the state realty transfer fee at that time. For a sale above $350,000 the state schedule charges $2.90 per $500 on the first $150,000, $4.25 per $500 from $150,000 to $200,000 and $4.80 per $500 from $200,000 to $550,000. Applied to a $400,000 sale, that works out to about $3,215, which is $870 plus $425 plus $1,920. Confirm the figure with your closing attorney, since senior, disabled and low-income rates are lower.

The county's recording schedule lists $30 for the first page of a deed, $10 for each added page, a $10 abstracting fee and a $5 homeless trust fund charge, with a $55 minimum. Camden County's online land records run from 1978 and the clerk's number is 856-225-5300. A New Jersey resident seller signs a residency certification at closing, while a nonresident prepays estimated income tax, so tell your attorney early if you are moving out of state.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection to sell a house in Cherry Hill?
faqs.a: Yes, two of them. The township requires a Certificate of Continued Occupancy for single-family resale, and the fire department requires a smoke alarm and carbon monoxide compliance certificate before settlement.

faqs.q: How much does the Cherry Hill resale inspection cost?
faqs.a: The occupancy inspection costs $100, due before the inspector arrives. The fire department sets its own fee schedule, which is posted on its checklist.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I book the Cherry Hill fire inspection?
faqs.a: Request it three to four weeks before settlement. The certificate is issued at the appointment if the home is compliant and payment is received, and temporary certificates are not given.

faqs.q: When are Cherry Hill taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. A ten-day grace period applies, and the payment has to reach the tax office by then because postmarks do not count.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Cherry Hill deed?
faqs.a: The Camden County Clerk records it. The schedule lists $30 for the first page of a deed, $10 for each added page, a $10 abstracting fee and a $5 homeless trust fund charge.
